sql_schemas: table employees | fields: id, employee_number, first_name, last_name, email, manager_id, department, hire_date, termination_date, employment_status, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at | pk: id | fks: manager_id -> employees.id | indexes: employee_number: unique lookup by employee number; email: unique lookup by email; manager_id: team hierarchy queries — find direct reports; employment_status: filter active/inactive/terminated employees

table leave_policies | fields: id, policy_name, leave_type, entitlement_days, accrual_rate, max_accumulation, minimum_notice_days, requires_manager_approval, is_active, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | indexes: leave_type: filter policies by leave type (annual, sick, emergency); is_active: filter active policies for entitlement lookups

table leave_requests | fields: id, employee_id, leave_policy_id, start_date, end_date, reason, status, approved_by, approved_at, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_policy_id -> leave_policies.id; approved_by -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id: look up all leave requests for an employee; status: filter by status (SUBMITTED, APPROVED, etc.); leave_policy_id: filter by leave type; start_date, end_date: date-range queries for calendar views and overlap detection; approved_by: find requests approved by a specific manager

table leave_balances | fields: id, employee_id, leave_policy_id, total_entitlement, used_days, remaining_days, fiscal_year, status, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_policy_id -> leave_policies.id | indexes: employee_id: look up balances for an employee; leave_policy_id: filter balances by policy; employee_id, fiscal_year: composite lookup — an employee's balance for a given fiscal year; employee_id, leave_policy_id, fiscal_year: unique constraint candidate — one balance row per employee/policy/year

table audit_logs | fields: id, entity_type, entity_id, action, old_values, new_values, performed_by, performed_at, ip_address, user_agent, created_at | pk: id | fks: performed_by -> employees.id | indexes: entity_type, entity_id: look up audit trail for a specific entity; performed_by: filter audit entries by actor; performed_at: time-range queries on audit history; action: filter by action type (CREATE, UPDATE, APPROVE, REJECT)

data_notes: Tables defined: employees, leave_policies, leave_requests, leave_balances, audit_logs. The leave_requests table uses leave_policy_id (not leave_type_id) to link to the policy that governs the request, consistent with the existing DOMAIN.md model. The leave_balances table uses a composite (employee_id, leave_policy_id, fiscal_year) as a logical unique constraint — one balance row per employee per policy per fiscal year. The audit_logs table is shared across all modules per GP-002; its schema is defined once here and referenced by name. All repository interfaces take an optional PoolClient parameter for transaction propagation.

open_questions.question: How are leave days counted when computing used_days from start_date to end_date? Are both dates inclusive? Are weekends and public holidays excluded?
open_questions.impact: Affects the balance deduction logic in the approval flow — the service that computes used_days before calling updateUsedDays on the balance repository. If the counting rule is wrong, balances will drift.
candidate_options: Business days + holiday calendar (requires a holiday table)

transaction_contract: Repository methods that participate in multi-step writes (create, updateStatus, updateUsedDays, upsert, create audit entry) accept an optional PoolClient parameter. When omitted, the method acquires a connection from the shared pool for that single operation. When provided, the method uses the caller's client. The calling service owns the unit of work: it acquires a client from the pool, executes BEGIN, passes the client to each participating repository method, then executes COMMIT on success or ROLLBACK on failure. The primary transactional scenario is leave approval: update leave_requests.status to APPROVED, update leave_balances.used_days/remaining_days, and insert an audit_logs row — all within a single transaction.
